title: Operator Shift Orchestra playbook and branded status bundles
author: Elena Park
content:
Summary
This playbook — the Operator Shift Orchestra — defines standardized shift choreography, quick-run runbooks for common LLM-serving issues, a compact postmortem scaffold, game-day exercises, and a set of 'branded' status bundles for customer-facing communication. It is intended for primary/secondary on-call operators, duty engineers, SREs, and customer success liaisons.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-stable for incidents affecting Redwood inference endpoints.
- Provide easy-to-graft customer status messages that are brand-safe and accurate.
- Standardize handoffs and retros to preserve institutional knowledge.
- Exercise shift teams with game-day scenarios that reflect production failure modes (latency spikes, KV cache corruption, quiet degradations).

Ownership and scope
- Owners: Eng SRE (primary), Serving Runtime (secondary), Customer Success (customer notices).
- Scope: All public inference endpoints, Dedicated pools, and Private control-plane integrations.
- Author: Elena Park (Runtime Ops).

Shift choreography (how an on-call shift should flow)
1) Pre-shift (30 minutes before start)
   - Read the daily shift brief (Slack #ops-brief). Check the overnight incident digest and any active P0/P1s.
   - Verify heartbeating dashboards are green: API success rate >= 99.5%, 95th percentile latency within SLO, queue depths stable.
2) Handover (first 10 minutes)
   - Run automated handoff checklist: list active incidents, outstanding runbook actions, recent escalations, ongoing game-day exercises.
   - Acknowledge handover in the shift log with a timestamp and short summary.
3) During shift
   - Monitor: Alerts, Service Health dashboard, and status-page watch.
   - Respond: Follow runbook containment steps for alerts. Escalate per matrix.
   - Triage windows: perform a short triage on high-noise alerts every 4 hours.
4) Handoff-out (end of shift)
   - Complete runbook actions or add clear next steps.
   - Write a 5-line summary and outstanding items; post to the shift log and mention the next on-call.

Shift rules and roles
- Primary: owns customer impact, initial mitigation, and RCA kickoff.
- Secondary: supports debugging, deep-dive tasks, and can act as bridge lead if Primary is out.
- Escalation lead: Engineering manager on-call for P0s (paged at 30 minutes without containment).
- Shift length: 8–12 hours depending on rota (team-specific). No more than 2 consecutive long shifts without rest.

Escalation matrix (quick view)
- P0 (global outage): Page Primary -> Secondary -> Escalation lead -> Exec oncall (if > 60m unresolved).
- P1 (regional service degradation): Page Primary -> Secondary -> Team SME.
- P2/P3: Slack alert to team channel; create ticket as needed.

Runbook templates (copyable, short)
1) API surge / sustained latency
   - Detect: 95th percentile latency > SLO for 5 minutes AND error rate increase > 0.5%.
   - Contain: 1) Enable throttling rule for non-synthetic traffic; 2) Ramp down batch sizes for background clients; 3) Fail over routing policy to cheaper region-variant if configured.
   - Validate: Confirm 95th percentile latency returns within SLO for 10 minutes.
   - Restore: Gradually remove throttles, monitor metrics for 30 minutes.
2) KV cache eviction / cold-cache storm
   - Detect: Sudden increase in model token processing time; cache hit-rate drops > 30%.
   - Contain: 1) Switch to pre-warmed model variant (if available); 2) Increase cache persistence retention on affected nodes; 3) Temporarily increase autoscaling target for runtime pool.
   - Validate: Cache hit-rate trends up and tail latency reduces.
   - Restore: Rollback autoscaling and persistence changes after 60–90 minutes of stable metrics.
3) Silent quality degradation (model output regressions)
   - Detect: Eval alert triggered for production prompt set OR customer report with clear regression signature.
   - Contain: 1) Route traffic to previous pinned model version; 2) Reduce sampling temperature for generation endpoints; 3) Engage model-onboarding lead.
   - Validate: Quality telemetry and sample prompts match expected guardrails.
   - Post-incident: Create a model regression postmortem and tagging.

Runbook checklist (short form)
- Triage: summary, severity, customer impact, affected region, model/version, endpoints.
- Containment steps taken (with timestamps).
- Evidence snapshot (metrics, request IDs, representative logs).
- Communications sent (internal and external).

Status page and customer-facing bundles
We use 'bundles' to ensure brand-safe, consistent language. Choose the smallest bundle appropriate for impact (A, B, C).
- Bundle A (Major outage, customer impact across regions)
  - Title: 'Service disruption: Redwood inference API'
  - Body: 'We are aware of elevated errors and sustained latency for Redwood inference endpoints. Our engineers are actively investigating and we will provide updates every 30 minutes. Customers may experience failures or timeouts during this period.'
  - Actions: update status every 30 minutes, post to support portal, and notify enterprise POCs via email.
  - Suggested severity badge: Major
- Bundle B (Partial regional degradation)
  - Title: 'Partial service degradation in <region>'
  - Body: 'We are experiencing increased latency for a subset of requests originating from <region>. We have applied mitigations and are monitoring. If your service is impacted, please open a support ticket and reference incident ID {INC_ID}.'
  - Actions: update every 60 minutes, targeted emails to affected customers.
- Bundle C (Informational / scheduled maintenance)
  - Title: 'Planned maintenance: <component>'
  - Body: 'We will perform scheduled maintenance affecting <component> on <date/time>. No action is required unless you rely on pinned private deployments; contact support for accommodation.'
  - Actions: pre-notice 72h and 24h, and post-completion note.

Customer message templates (email + status snippet)
- Short status snippet (for status.redwood.com): 'We are investigating increased latency impacting inference calls in <region>. Our team has applied mitigations. Next update: <ETA>.'
- Enterprise email (first notification)
  Subject: 'Redwood Incident {INC_ID}: Service impact affecting inference requests'
  Body: 'Hello — We are currently investigating elevated error rates and latency affecting inference requests. Impacted customers may see failures or delays. Our team has applied initial mitigations and is working on full restoration. We will send an update in 30 minutes or sooner. If you have high-priority workloads, please reply and include your region and sample request IDs.'

Postmortem scaffold (compact)
- Title/Incident ID
- Timeline (UTC) — include detection, mitigation, and resolution timestamps
- Impact summary — customers, services, data-plane / control-plane effects
- Root cause (summary)
- Contributing factors
- Corrective actions (owners and due dates)
- Learnings and follow-up (A/B test or rollout policy changes)

Game-day exercises (90 minute template)
1) Objective: Practice coordinated triage for a silent degradation that requires model rollback.
2) Roles: Bridge lead, Primary on-call, Secondary, Customer liaison, Observability SME.
3) Scenario: Synthetic evals flag a 5% regression for a high-traffic prompt set; customers start reporting quality issues.
4) Tasks and scoring: 1) Detection within 10 minutes (3 pts). 2) Containment (model rollback) within 25 minutes (5 pts). 3) Brand-safe customer update posted within 30 minutes (2 pts). 4) Post-exercise quick retro completed within 24 hours (1 pt).
5) Debrief: run through what went well, what blocked, and actions assigned.

Shift log template (example entry)
- Timestamp: 2025-06-14T08:04Z
- Operator: @elena.park
- Active incidents: INC-2025-1123 (P1) — API latency in eu-west1
- Actions this shift: toggled throttling for background clients 08:15Z; engaged serving-runtime team 08:30Z
- Outstanding items for next shift: follow up on autoscaling tuning; validate canary traffic profile.

Evidence capture requirements (for P0/P1)
- Minimum evidence bundle: 1) Grafana snapshot for 1h pre/post; 2) 10 representative request IDs; 3) Bridge transcript or log excerpt; 4) Any customer reports or support tickets.

Retention and governance
- Runbooks: review cadence 6 months.
- Shift logs: retained for 2 years.
- Postmortems: retained permanently; action items tracked in Jira and closed with evidence.

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets and debug hints
- Export sample request IDs (example): curl -X POST https://internal-api/services/requests/query -d '{"filter":"status:\"error\"","limit":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- Quick model rollback (internal CLI): rwoodctl deploy rollback --service inference --to-version v2025-03-01 --region eu-west1

Frequently asked questions
Q: When should Customer Success draft an email vs. posting to the status page?
A: Use status page for broad incidents. Draft an email when the incident affects enterprise customers or when follow-up actions are required (credits, post-incident briefings).
